snippet.title: Meet the healers who say they have a 'gift from God' | Unreported World
snippet.description:
Unreported World is from the Philippines investigating the controversial world of spiritual healers. Sahar Zand examines whether the popular practice is a blessing or a curse.
 
Across the country, with high medical costs and difficulties accessing healthcare, patients put their trust in alternative treatments to cure anything from chronic pain to cancer. Faith healers, blending Catholic rituals with centuries-old traditions, promise miraculous recoveries through prayer and herbal remedies.
 
On the outskirts of Manilla, we meet three faith healers claiming to treat over one hundred people per week. They believe they are divinely chosen to cure conditions modern medicine can’t detect. Their ritualistic, sometimes disturbing rituals, have earned them a loyal following, and an income derived from donations, socials media followers and faith healing accessories. 
 
But critics warn the industry is dangerously unregulated. Medical professionals fear patients are being misled, delaying vital treatment with often fatal consequences. Zand hears from those who believe their loved ones paid the ultimate price, after putting their trust in miracle cures that they now believe were a scam.

And a warning, there are some scenes of ritualistic ceremonies, some viewers may find upsetting.

snippet.title: Walk The Bayonet Charge With Me At Gettysburg | Civil War (No AI)
snippet.description:
The Bayonet Charge That Saved The Battle Of Gettysburg?

What really happened when Joshua Chamberlain ordered the 20th Maine Infantry Regiment to fix bayonets at the Battle of Gettysburg?
By the late afternoon of July 2nd, the Union left flank at Little Round Top was stretched thin. Ammunition was nearly exhausted. Confederate assaults were probing for a breakthrough.
In this episode, we move beyond legend and examine the tactical realities:
• The terrain constraints on Little Round Top
• The regiment’s ammunition state
• The envelopment threat on the Union left
• Why a downhill bayonet charge may have been the only viable option
Was this calculated manoeuvre warfare — or a controlled collapse turned counterattack?
Standing on the ground itself, we reconstruct the angles, timing, and battlefield geometry to assess whether the charge was decisive… or simply the best option available in a deteriorating situation.

snippet.title: Archeologists Discover A Perfectly Preserved Medieval Shipwreck
snippet.description:
Locked deep beneath the waterlogged shingle of a Kent quarry, an exceptionally preserved 16th-century shipwreck has finally reemerged. Weighing over 150 tons and measuring more than 25 meters long, this rare Elizabethan vessel offers marine archaeologists a once-in-a-lifetime glimpse into Tudor shipwright craft. Plus, hidden beneath the floorboards of the Tower of London, archaeologists have uncovered the ruins of Henry VIII's secret assay house. This discovery reveals the industrial-scale fraud orchestrated by the king himself to debase British currency with copper, earning him the nickname "Old Coppernose."
